- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots downward in the following days; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged sell-off bias.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion toward historical range, model tends to overpredict extreme moves; dampen forecast volatility in mid-term horizon.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize momentum reversal; increase forecast slope slightly to reflect sentiment-driven rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently underestimates upward momentum in early days of a rally; shift forecast upward by 1–2% in first 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals, model tends to overfit to recent noise; smooth forecast transitions and avoid abrupt directional shifts.
